items.description: one element per PRICED LINE in the two-column net price list. Every line that ends in a right-justified decimal price is its own item, including each successive size/unit line printed beneath a form. Read the full left column top-to-bottom, then the full right column. Do not merge multiple priced lines into one item and do not skip any priced line.

article.description: the base article name from the bold ALL-CAPS header that begins the group this line belongs to (the header printed at the far left, often followed by a dash). Repeat this exact header text on EVERY priced line in the group, including all indented form and size sub-lines, until the next bold ALL-CAPS header appears. Copy it verbatim in the printed capitalization without the trailing dash.

form.description: the full preparation/variety qualifier in force for this priced line, excluding the bold article header and the 'per ...' unit. Build it from the qualifier text that governs the line: if the line sits under a variety/type sub-heading (a descriptor that itself begins a sub-group of forms), include that governing sub-heading followed by the line's own descriptor, as printed (for example a variety heading combined with a physical-form word). Copy all qualifier text verbatim in printed order. When a priced line shows only a 'per ...' unit and no new descriptor, repeat the full qualifier that governs it. Use an empty string when the governing line carries a price with no qualifier at all.

size.description: the quantity/unit basis that the price applies to on this line — the 'per ...' phrase printed immediately left of the price (the weight, volume, count, or pack unit). Copy it verbatim including any fraction and unit abbreviation (for example a per-pound, per-fractional-pound, per-ounce, per-pint, per-gram, or per-vial basis). Empty string only if genuinely absent.

price.description: the right-justified decimal amount printed at the end of this line, as a number with no currency symbol. A price printed with a leading decimal point and no leading zero is a value below one dollar.
